# Forest Lab / tree-visualizer — codebase report

**Forest Lab** is a Next.js 16 + React 19 teaching demo that shows how a random forest bags data, grows Gini trees, walks samples, and majority-votes — with a guided tour and stage-driven UI.

---

## 1. File structure overview

```
tree-visualizer/
├── app/
│   ├── page.tsx              → renders <ForestDemo />
│   ├── layout.tsx            → fonts (Fraunces/Nunito), metadata
│   └── globals.css           → design tokens, page background
├── components/
│   ├── forest/               → demo domain UI
│   │   ├── ForestDemo.tsx    → orchestration / state machine
│   │   ├── ScatterPlot.tsx   → 2D sample points
│   │   ├── TreeView.tsx      → SVG decision tree
│   │   ├── EnsembleMerge.tsx → vote bars / merge animation
│   │   └── StageSidebar.tsx  → stage copy + jump nav
│   ├── walkthrough/
│   │   └── WalkthroughPortal.tsx → spotlight coachmarks
│   └── ui/
│       ├── Button.tsx, Header.tsx, Slider.tsx
│       ├── Stack.tsx, Tooltip.tsx (HelpHint)
├── lib/forest/               → ML + demo content (no UI)
│   ├── types.ts              → data model
│   ├── dataset.ts            → toy leaf generator + RNG
│   ├── tree.ts               → CART-ish grow (Gini)
│   ├── forest.ts             → bagging, train, predict
│   ├── layout.ts             → tidy tree layout
│   ├── stages.ts             → stage copy
│   └── tour.ts               → tour step definitions
└── package.json              → next@16.2.12, react@19, no ML libs
```

Entry: `app/page.tsx` → `ForestDemo`. All ML is pure TypeScript in `lib/forest/`.

---

## 2. What the demo does

Guided Random Forest story over a 2-feature, 3-class “leaf” dataset (Oak / Maple / Pine):

| Stage | Id | What you see |
|-------|-----|--------------|
| 1 | `data` | Scatter of labeled points |
| 2 | `bootstrap` | Bag vs OOB highlighting on scatter |
| 3
